## In one sentence

Heredity explains how traits are transmitted, while phylogeny describes
relationships through common ancestry.

## Genes, alleles, and traits

A gene is a region of hereditary material; alleles are alternative forms of a
gene. Phenotypes arise from genes and environments, often together. A heritable
trait is not necessarily fixed: its expression can depend on conditions and
development.

For a simple diploid locus, an individual's genotype contains two alleles. A
population's allele frequencies can change through selection, drift, mutation,
and gene flow. Evolution is measured in populations across generations, not in
an individual's response during its lifetime.

## Reading a phylogenetic tree

A phylogenetic tree represents hypotheses about branching history. Nodes mark
inferred common ancestors; sister groups share the most recent common ancestor.
Rotating a branch around a node does not change relationships. A trait shared
because of common ancestry is a homology; a similar trait that evolved
independently is an analogy or homoplasy.

::: {.callout-important}
The left-to-right order of tips is not a time axis. Read relationships from the
branching pattern and common ancestors, not from visual proximity alone.
:::

## Check your understanding

Draw a tree for four taxa. Mark the most recent common ancestor of two sister
taxa and identify one character that could provide evidence for the tree.
